content.text: {"what_it_is":{"claims":[{"text":"JSF STOVL is the Navy-managed procurement line for the F-35B, the Short Take-Off and Vertical Landing (STOVL) variant of the Joint Strike Fighter (JSF) family of aircraft. The Joint Strike Fighter program fields three variants: the F-35A Conventional Take Off and Landing (CTOL) version, the F-35B STOVL version, and the F-35C Carrier Variant (CV), sharing commonality to minimize life-cycle costs.","citation":{"fact_id":"f0d765b03beeee18"}},{"text":"This is a joint program with no executive service; Service Acquisition Executive authority alternates between the Department of the Navy and the Department of the Air Force and currently resides with the Navy. It is described as a Commandant of the Marine Corps Force Design program.","citation":{"fact_id":"f0d765b03beeee18"}},{"text":"For the Marine Corps, the F-35B combines precision weapons and multi-spectral sensors with the expeditionary responsiveness of a STOVL fighter-attack platform. The Marine Corps currently has seven F-35B operational squadrons and will stand up an additional five.","citation":{"fact_id":"f0d765b03beeee18"}},{"text":"Initial Operational Capability occurred in July 2015, and the Full Rate Production decision occurred in March 2024 after completion of Initial Operational Test and Evaluation.","citation":{"fact_id":"f0d765b03beeee18"}},{"text":"The funding falls under the Aircraft Procurement, Navy account (Exhibit P-1).","citation":{"fact_id":"ee4a0842dfc79225"}}]},"why_it_matters":{"claims":[{"text":"The FY 2026 budget provides funding for 11 F-35B aircraft plus associated non-recurring and ancillary mission equipment, and supports advanced procurement, squadron stand-up, training, and logistics requirements.","citation":{"fact_id":"4a166b96799797f9"}},{"text":"For fiscal year 2024, actual spending on JSF STOVL was about $2.32 billion (2,319,442 USD thousands).","citation":{"fact_id":"ee4a0842dfc79225"}},{"text":"For fiscal year 2025, enacted funding was about $2.14 billion (2,141,076 USD thousands).","citation":{"fact_id":"26dde8e930db35c8"}},{"text":"The FY 2026 request totals about $1.90 billion (1,901,057 USD thousands), a decrease from both the FY 2024 actual and the FY 2025 enacted levels.","citation":{"fact_id":"fbc00c61da4dcaad"}},{"text":"The FY 2026 request was reduced by $1.653 million for Advisory and Assistance Services in alignment with Executive Order 14222, the President's Department of Government Efficiency Cost Efficiency Initiative.","citation":{"fact_id":"4a166b96799797f9"}},{"text":"FY 2026 funding also supports transitioning the Autonomic Logistics Information System (ALIS) to the F-35 Operational Data Integrated Network (ODIN), a modern logistics and information system, and continued depot activation to expand long-term sustainment repair capacity.","citation":{"fact_id":"4a166b96799797f9"}},{"text":"Cumulative funding for all prior years is reported at about $26.36 billion (26,361.229 USD millions).","citation":{"fact_id":"60a445ceba81156b"}}]},"players":{"claims":[{"text":"The program is managed by the Department of the Navy (organization code N), with Service Acquisition Executive authority currently residing with the Navy.","citation":{"fact_id":"f0d765b03beeee18"}},{"text":"FY 2026 support costs include equipment for squadron completion at Marine Corps Air Station Beaufort (VMFA-224) and Marine Corps Air Station Cherry Point (VMFA-231), and air vehicle modification support at Fleet Readiness Center Southeast.","citation":{"fact_id":"4a166b96799797f9"}}]},"recent_developments":{"claims":[]}}
